📌 Tehran, IRNA – Hezbollah carries out a drone attack on an Israeli military patrol in the Ali al-Taher Heights in southern Lebanon, according to Lebanese media reports.

A report by the Lebanese Al Mayadeen TV indicated that the Lebanese resistance fighters spotted an Israeli military vehicle climbing toward the Ali al-Taher Heights at around 1 a.m. local time on Wednesday.
​
It added that the Hezbollah fighters launched several FPV drones toward the vehicle after it reached the area, with one drone striking the vehicle directly and putting it out of service.
​
Meanwhile, the Israeli military claimed that Hezbollah had launched two suicide drones toward Israeli soldiers positioned in the Ali al-Taher Heights.
​
The Rased news network also reported that the Israeli military shelled the Ali al-Taher Heights with artillery.
​
In a separate development, the Israeli military carried out artillery and airstrikes against the southern Lebanese towns of Al-Mansouri, Zawtar al-Sharqiya and Arabsalim.
​
At the same time, Israeli military drones flew over Beirut’s southern Dahiyeh area, the city of Beirut and the coastline stretching from Ramlieh to Khaldeh.
​
The fighting in southern Lebanon has continued despite a so-called ceasefire between Lebanon and the Israeli regime.
​
Israeli forces have continued bombing villages and towns in southern Lebanon and carrying out widespread destruction of homes and public facilities.
​
In response, Hezbollah has continued confronting Israeli violations of the ceasefire with fire, killing or wounding a number of Israeli soldiers and destroying Israeli military equipment, according to the report.
​
The latest attacks come amid continued Israeli military incursion against southern Lebanon.
​
Thousands of Lebanese civilians – including hundreds of children, women and first responders – have been killed since March in Israeli military attacks despite its claims of only targeting Hezbollah personnel and infrastructure.

🔊 Putin, Pezeshkian discussed nuclear cooperation at Bishkek meeting: Rosatom chief

📌 Moscow, IRNA – The CEO of Russia’s state-owned nuclear corporation Rosatom says the recent meeting between President Vladimir Putin and his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek included bilateral issues, including the two countries' cooperation in the nuclear field.

Alexey Likhachev made the revelation on Wednesday on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum, which is held each year in Vladivostok, in order to encourage and attract foreign investment in the Russian Far East.
​
He said that Putin and Pezeshkian met face-to-face during the SCO Summit in Kyrgyzstan on Tuesday, discussing nuclear cooperation and reviewing the status of the Bushehr nuclear power plant, in the wake of the joint US-Israeli war of aggression against Iran.
​
Likhachev stated that the situation at the plant was calm, adding that Rosatom specialists were preparing to participate in planned maintenance for Unit 1 of the Bushehr plant, scheduled for mid-September.
​
He noted that the maintenance work involved replacing a portion of the fuel assemblies, confirming that the necessary nuclear fuel for the refueling cycle had already been delivered to the site.
​
Stating that Tehran and Moscow had previously signed agreements on the construction of another site for large nuclear power plants, the CEO of Rosatom said Iranian officials had also raised the issue of building smaller plants in previous negotiations.
​
Rosatom, which operates the plant in collaboration with Iranian specialists and is currently constructing two additional units at the site, had previously evacuated hundreds of Russian personnel following the launch of the US-Israeli war on Iran on February 28.
​
During an interview last year, Likhachev had confirmed that his company was planning to build two nuclear power plant units – each with a capacity of 1,000 megawatts – adjacent to the first unit of the Bushehr plant, and the construction process was progressing.

🎙 Iranian parliament deputy speaker condemns US attack on wedding ceremony in Sirik

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad has condemned a US attack on a wedding ceremony in Kuhestak, Sirik County, describing it as a continuation of the attacks on Minab and Lamerd on February 28, 2026, and saying Washington is seeking to disrupt everyday life in Iran.

Addressing a virtual parliamentary session on Wednesday, Nikzad said Iran had demonstrated resilience in the face of military pressure and aggression, stressing that national unity and public calm must be protected.
​
He said Parliament and the government must strengthen hope, prevent social polarization, and ensure the country’s resistance is reflected in economic conditions, employment, housing, healthcare, and production.
​
Nikzad also stressed that Iran’s strength extends beyond military capabilities to its people, scientists, workers, farmers, teachers, doctors, engineers and entrepreneurs. He called for stronger economic foundations alongside defense capabilities.
​
Referring to the Strait of Hormuz, he said its circumstances would not return to those before the war and argued that the issue had no military solution.
​
Nikzad further condemned the attack on the wedding ceremony and said that such actions would strengthen national unity and resistance. At the end of his speech, lawmakers expressed their resentment over US acts of aggression against Iran.
